subject: general
question: The Kanjira is a frame drum of South India. It consists of a skin (usually iguana) stretched and pasted on a circular ________ frame.
solution:
The correct answer is __**wooden**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kanjira **

 
 
• The** frame drum known as the kanjira (Khanjari) **originates from **South India and belongs to the tambourine family**.
 
• It consists of a skin (usually iguana) stretched and pasted on a **circular wooden frame**.
 
• In the **side of the frame**, there are frequently** three or four slots where bell-metal jingle discs** **are hung from metal crossbars**.
 
• The **khanjari and kanjani **of North and East India and Nepal are related to the term kanjira.
 
• **Wetting the skin** allows the kanjira to be tuned to **different pitches**.
 
• The **right hand's fingers** are used to **beat it** while it is **being held at the bottom of the frame by the left hand**, which also adjusts the** skin's tension**.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://www.indianetzone.com/photos_gallery/33/Kanjira_23286.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This instrument has a** monitor lizard skin drumhead** covering one side and is left open on the other.
 
• It has been used for many years in **India as a folk and bhajan instrument**.
 
• **Manpoondia Pillai **is credited with the **invention of the modern form of the kanjira **as well as the **instrument's introduction into South Indian Carnatic music**.
 
• Kanjira is known as **Khaijadi in Nepal**.
 
• In addition to the Khaijadi, the **Daanf, Damphu, and Hring tambourines **are also played in **Nepal**.
